content:
Inverse trig looks small on the syllabus, yet JEE loves it. One clean identity can turn a scary expression into a single step. So the marks here come fast, if you know the rules. Try the free JEE Inverse Trigonometry online test below. It holds 15 solved MCQs with instant scoring. Aim for 12 right.

What JEE asks from inverse trigonometry

  • Principal values of arcsin, arccos and arctan.
  • Sums of two arctans, so the addition rule matters.
  • Values like tan of arcsin, and sin of arccos.
  • Ranges where a chosen identity still holds.
  • Maximum and minimum of squared inverse expressions.
  • Simple equations that hide inside an inverse function.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Use arctan a + arctan b = arctan((a+b)/(1−ab)) when ab stays below 1.
  • Recall that arcsin x plus arccos x always equals pi over 2.
  • For sin of arccos x, take root of 1 minus x squared.
  • For tan of arcsin x, take x over root of 1 minus x squared.
  • Keep arctan x plus arccot x fixed at pi over 2 as well.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Forgetting the domain, and so picking a wrong branch.
  • Adding two arctans when the product ab exceeds 1.
  • Mixing up range limits for arcsin against arccos.
  • Dropping the sign of x inside a square root step.
